lesson.beat.builds.alt: Seasons two and three. Path A’s skill bars rise faster than before, with arrows showing ball control helping passing and passing helping positioning. Path B’s bars rise slowly.
lesson.beat.builds.body1: Path A Maya stops staring at the ball. Now she can look up and see her teammates. So passing gets easier to learn.
lesson.beat.builds.body2: Each skill gives the next one a place to stand. Path B Maya is still working on the basics, so the gap grows.
lesson.beat.builds.heading: Then learning builds on learning.
lesson.beat.closed.alt: Rain clouds over the ridge. The lake trail beyond the bridge is marked closed. A ranger stands at the bridge.
lesson.beat.closed.body1: Last night, a storm washed part of the lake trail away. A ranger at the bridge says it’s closed. No plan can stop the rain.
lesson.beat.closed.heading: Something they couldn’t control.
lesson.beat.closed.option.ask: Ask the ranger about other trails
lesson.beat.closed.option.ask.feedback: The ranger smiles. “Have you seen the Waterfall Trail? It’s shorter, and it’s open.” A lucky tip they never planned for.
lesson.beat.closed.option.home.feedback: Feeling disappointed is normal. Alfredo feels it too, and going home is allowed. But is there another good choice?
lesson.beat.closed.option.sneak.feedback: The sign is there because the trail isn’t safe. Sneaking past could turn a bad day into a dangerous one.
lesson.beat.cover.alt: A single dot marks the beginning of a life.
lesson.beat.cover.body1: Your choices shape where a life can go. So do things nobody chooses, the lucky ones and the unlucky ones.
lesson.beat.cover.body2: Take your time. First you’ll join a hike and meet a girl with two paths. Then you’ll play a game and try out a whole life.
lesson.beat.cover.heading: The paths we make
lesson.beat.explore.alt: An interactive map of example life choices. At each fork, two or three choices branch ahead. Some close for a reason; some lucky chances open. The chosen path turns dark green, with gray branches for choices not taken.
lesson.beat.explore.body1: Start at the beginning and pick a choice at each fork. Some doors close, and some open by surprise. You can always go back.
lesson.beat.explore.heading: Choose a life path.
lesson.beat.fork.alt: One path splits into two. Path A: Maya keeps practising. Path B: Maya mostly skips.
lesson.beat.fork.body1: Meet Maya. She’s eight, and she just joined a soccer team.
lesson.beat.fork.body2: Let’s imagine two ways her next three years could go. Same Maya, same start. Only her choices are different.
lesson.beat.fork.heading: Same start, two paths.
lesson.beat.game.alt: A game of ten afternoons. Each afternoon has three choices. Skill boxes for soccer and cello, and an energy meter, show what builds up.
lesson.beat.game.body1: You play soccer and you’re learning the cello. You have ten afternoons after school. Choose what to do with each one, and watch what builds up.
lesson.beat.game.body2: Rest counts too. When you’re worn out, practice doesn’t stick as well.
lesson.beat.game.heading: Ten afternoons, two skills.
lesson.beat.halfway.alt: The walkers climb to the big rock. Their water bottles are half full, and the lake is still far away.
lesson.beat.halfway.body1: Partway up, Alfredo checks his bottle. Half the water is gone already. The lake is still far away.
lesson.beat.halfway.heading: Half the water is gone.
lesson.beat.halfway.option.continue.feed: They’d reach the lake with almost no water for the long walk home. On a hot day, that’s dangerous. Dad says, “The lake isn’t going anywhere. Let’s turn back.”
lesson.beat.halfway.option.turn.feedback: Good thinking. The other half of the water is for getting home safely.
lesson.beat.many.alt: Hundreds of green paths branch out from one starting dot and spread across the map.
lesson.beat.many.body1: Each line is one way a life could go. Lines split and bend and cross. Nobody walks them all. Nobody needs to.
lesson.beat.many.heading: A life can go many ways.
lesson.beat.never-late.alt: Both Mayas practise basketball for a season. Path B’s calendar fills for the first time and her bars rise; Path A keeps her head start.
lesson.beat.never-late.body1: Path B Maya can start practising any season she likes. When she does, her skills grow too. She has more to catch up on, but the door is still open.
lesson.beat.never-late.body2: Real life is messier than this picture. Coaches, time and money matter. Luck does too, and sometimes luck is kind: someone spots you and says, “Keep going.” Practice helps, but it doesn’t guarantee a result.
lesson.beat.never-late.heading: It’s never too late to start.
lesson.beat.outside.alt: A few paths ahead are marked closed, with reasons such as a full team or a cancelled class. Many others stay open.
lesson.beat.outside.body1: Other people and luck shape your path too. Sometimes a way closes, and nobody chose that. Sometimes a door opens that you never knocked on.
lesson.beat.outside.body2: A teacher notices you. A friend invites you along. Your choices matter. They’re just not the whole story. Let’s zoom in on one stretch of path.
lesson.beat.outside.heading: Not everything is yours to choose.
lesson.beat.plan.alt: A trail map: the trail climbs from the trailhead through a forest, past a stream and up a ridge to Mirror Lake. Alfredo and his dad wait at the trailhead with full water bottles.
lesson.beat.plan.body1: Alfredo and his dad are getting ready for a big hike. They study the map. Then they pack snacks, jackets and a bottle of water each.
lesson.beat.plan.body2: Mirror Lake is a long way up. Nobody gets there in one jump. It’s one small step after another.
lesson.beat.plan.heading: Alfredo makes a plan.
lesson.beat.practice.alt: Three short practice loops appear near home, one after another. The backpack gains three cards: Reading the map, Spotting landmarks, Resting before you’re tired.
lesson.beat.practice.body1: Over the next few weeks, they take short walks near home. Alfredo practises reading the map. He learns to spot landmarks. Those are things you can see from far away, like a big rock.
lesson.beat.practice.body2: Each walk starts from what he learned on the last one. His dad helps too. Learning with someone counts.
lesson.beat.practice.heading: Practice builds on practice.
lesson.beat.respond.alt: The walkers follow the open Waterfall Trail to a lookout beside a waterfall.
lesson.beat.respond.body1: They take the Waterfall Trail and eat lunch by the falls. Alfredo says it’s the best sandwich of his life. The lake can wait.
lesson.beat.respond.body2: That’s called resilience. You can’t control everything, but you can find a good way forward.
lesson.beat.respond.closer.body1: No. Turning back, resting, asking for help or picking a new goal can all be good choices.
lesson.beat.respond.closer.body2: Alfredo can feel disappointed and still decide what to do next. Nobody has to pretend a setback feels good.
lesson.beat.respond.closer.heading: Does resilience mean never stopping?
lesson.beat.respond.heading: Plans change. You can respond.
lesson.beat.retry.alt: The walkers climb past the place where they turned back last time. They have plenty of water and reach the bridge over the stream.
lesson.beat.retry.body1: This time they carry more water and plan where to rest. Alfredo spots the big rock and the stream from the map.
lesson.beat.retry.body2: They aren’t starting from zero. Everything they learned comes with them.
lesson.beat.retry.heading: The second try.
lesson.beat.slow.alt: Season one. Path A’s calendar is mostly filled; Path B’s has a few practices. Both sets of skill bars are low, with Path A slightly ahead.
lesson.beat.slow.body1: In her first season, Path A Maya goes to most practices. At home, she kicks a ball against the wall. Path B Maya goes now and then.
lesson.beat.slow.body2: After one season, the difference is small. Early practice often feels like nothing is happening. Something is.
lesson.beat.slow.heading: At first, progress feels slow.
lesson.beat.sort.alt: Six cards sorted into two groups. Their choices: how much water to pack, turning back, practising with the map, asking the ranger. Outside their control: the storm, and a friendly ranger being there.
lesson.beat.sort.body1: Sort each card. Was it their choice, or something outside their control? Outside things can be bad luck or good luck.
lesson.beat.sort.heading: What was in their control?
lesson.beat.takeaways.alt: The life map comes back, with the traveller at Today and many light green paths still open ahead.
lesson.beat.takeaways.body1: Your choices matter. They’re just not the whole story. Lots of paths are still open. What will you practise next?
lesson.beat.takeaways.heading: What to take with you.
lesson.beat.transfer.alt: Both skill boxes switch to basketball. Path A starts with part of Court sense and Passing already filled, carried across from soccer. Dribbling starts low for both. Path B starts low on all three.
lesson.beat.transfer.body1: At eleven, both Mayas try basketball. It’s a different ball, and dribbling with your hands is new.
lesson.beat.transfer.body2: But Path A Maya already knows where to stand and when to pass. That comes with her. Path B Maya has to learn most of it from the start.
lesson.beat.transfer.heading: Trying something new.
lesson.beat.travel.alt: A dot travels from the start to Today, at age 12. Labels name some choices: dark ones taken on the way, gray ones not taken, and green ones still possible ahead.
lesson.beat.travel.body1: Here’s someone who is twelve. The dark line is the path they took. At each fork they picked one way, and the others turned gray.
lesson.beat.travel.body2: The green paths ahead are still open. What they learn and practise now gets them ready for some of those paths.
lesson.beat.travel.heading: We travel one path at a time.
lesson.beat.turnback.alt: The walkers return to the trailhead. A new card in the backpack reads: Water for there and back.
lesson.beat.turnback.body1: They walk home without seeing the lake. Alfredo is disappointed. So is his dad.
lesson.beat.turnback.body2: But they learned something for next time: bring enough water to get there and back.
lesson.beat.turnback.heading: Turning back isn’t giving up.
lesson.sort.ask: Asking the ranger about other trails
lesson.sort.done: They couldn’t choose the storm. They couldn’t choose a friendly ranger either. They could choose how to pack, when to turn back, what to practise and who to ask.
lesson.sort.progress: {count} of {total} sorted. Drag each card to a side, or tap Skip to see the answers.
lesson.sort.ranger: A friendly ranger at the bridge
lesson.takeaway.add.heading: Choices add up.
lesson.takeaway.add.text: Small things you do again and again can grow into something big, for better or worse. One hard day doesn’t decide your future.
lesson.takeaway.build.heading: Learning builds on learning.
lesson.takeaway.build.text: What you know gives the next thing a place to start. Sometimes that works even for something new.
lesson.takeaway.weather.heading: Not everything is yours to choose.
lesson.takeaway.weather.text: Some surprises are storms. Some are lucky breaks. Either way, you can pause, ask for help and choose your next step.
